goals.description: Identify the requested database change, current schema and migration history, production constraints, database engine, ORM or migration tool, and whether the change touches schema, data, indexes, application code, or deployment sequencing.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus only on understanding the migration task and project context. Determine the database, migration tooling, existing migration conventions, target tables/columns/indexes, whether production scale or zero downtime matters, and whether any deployed migrations must be treated as immutable.
goals.name: inspect migration context

goals.description: Design the migration approach before editing files, separating schema and data work, selecting any expand-contract phases, and deciding which tool workflow to use.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Create a concrete migration plan from the inspected context. Keep DDL and DML in separate migrations, avoid editing already-deployed migrations, prefer forward fixes for rollback, and use expand-contract sequencing for renames, drops, and other production-sensitive changes.
goals.name: plan safe migration sequence

goals.description: Use the project’s migration system to create or locate the needed migration files, including empty/custom migrations where the ORM cannot express required safe SQL.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Work only on creating or selecting the migration files/artifacts required by the plan. Follow the detected tool’s conventions, such as Prisma, Drizzle, Django, TypeORM, golang-migrate, or raw SQL migrations. Do not apply production migrations here unless explicitly required by the user.
goals.name: create migration scaffolding

goals.description: Implement table, column, and constraint changes using production-safe patterns such as nullable or defaulted new columns, separate constraint tightening, and delayed destructive operations.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on schema DDL other than standalone index work. Add columns safely, avoid NOT NULL without a default on existing large tables, avoid destructive drops before application code is ready, and express renames as additive changes when zero downtime is needed.
goals.name: implement safe schema changes

goals.description: Add, modify, or remove indexes using non-blocking database-specific techniques where needed, especially concurrent index creation on existing PostgreSQL tables.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus only on index-related migration work. For existing production tables, avoid blocking writes; use database-specific concurrent or online index operations when supported, and handle tool restrictions such as PostgreSQL CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY not running inside a transaction.
goals.name: implement safe index changes

goals.description: Create a separate data migration or backfill when data must be populated, transformed, or synchronized, using batching and progress-safe patterns for large tables.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus only on data migration work. Keep it separate from schema DDL, avoid one huge transaction on large tables, use batched updates or framework equivalents, and define the reverse behavior or mark the data migration intentionally irreversible when appropriate.
goals.name: implement separate data migration

goals.description: Update ORM schemas, generated clients, and application read/write behavior to match the migration sequence, including dual-write or delayed-drop behavior for zero-downtime changes.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on application and ORM-side changes required by the migration plan. For expand-contract changes, ensure the app writes both old and new fields when required, later reads from the new field, and removes references before any column/table is dropped.
goals.name: coordinate application changes

goals.description: Ensure migrations include DOWN steps where the tool expects them or are explicitly marked irreversible, and document the forward-recovery or rollback plan.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on rollback and recovery readiness. Add or review DOWN migrations where applicable, avoid relying on editing deployed migrations, and document how to recover using a new forward migration when production rollback is unsafe or not intended.
goals.name: define rollback and recovery

goals.description: Run or document the appropriate migration checks and tests, including generation/status commands, production-scale testing expectations, lock-safety review, and final safety checklist verification.
goals.goal_entering_prompt: Focus on validation only. Run the relevant migration/tool commands when safe, regenerate ORM clients if required, check migration status, review for full-table locks and mixed DDL/DML, and confirm the safety checklist before considering the migration ready.
goals.name: validate migration safety
